subject: general
question: In April 2025, Chief Justice Sanjiv Khanna named _____ as his successor, who will be the _____ upon appointment

options.text: Justice B R Gavai; 53rd Chief Justice of India
Justice B R Gavai; 52ⁿd Chief Justice of India
Justice Hima Kohli; 53rd Chief Justice of India
Justice Surya Kant; 51st Chief Justice of India

solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice B R Gavai; 52nd Chief Justice of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Justice Sanjiv Khanna, the 51st Chief Justice of India**, retired in May 2025, as per the standard retirement age of 65 for Supreme Court judges.
 
• **Justice B R Gavai** has been named as his successor, making him the **52nd Chief Justice of India** upon appointment.
 
• Justice B R Gavai is known for his significant contributions to the judiciary and has been part of several landmark judgments during his tenure in the Supreme Court.
 
• He will be the second Chief Justice of India from the Scheduled Caste community, following Justice K G Balakrishnan, who served as the 37th CJI.
 
• The appointment of the Chief Justice of India is made by the President of India based on seniority among the Supreme Court judges and recommendations from the outgoing CJI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Justice of India (CJI):**

 
 
• The Chief Justice of India is the head of the judiciary system and the Supreme Court, the highest constitutional court in India.
 
• The CJI plays a vital role in upholding the Constitution, interpreting laws, and maintaining checks and balances between the three branches of government.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility for the CJI:**
 
 
• Must be a citizen of India.
 
• Must have served as a judge in a High Court for at least five years or as an advocate in a High Court for at least ten years, or be a distinguished jurist in the President's opinion.
 
 
 
• **Appointment Process:**
 
 
• The President of India appoints the CJI based on seniority among the judges of the Supreme Court.
 
• The outgoing CJI recommends their successor in consultation with other senior judges of the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **Retirement Age:**
 
 
• Supreme Court judges, including the CJI, retire at the age of 65.
 
• High Court judges, by comparison, retire at the age of 62.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Justice H J Kania was the first Chief Justice of India, serving from 1950 to 1951.
 
• Justice Fathima Beevi was the first woman to be appointed as a Supreme Court judge in India, paving the way for greater representation in the judiciary.
